title: A quiet favour at the library
summary: Copy the member card file from Tallis Library.
brief:
A small library in Lisbon keeps a list of who borrows what. I would like to read it.

Copy member_cards.dat from their system. Nobody is watching that machine closely, so this is a good one to learn on. Payment on delivery.

title: Lose the ledger
summary: Delete the bandwidth ledger at Kestrel Community Net.
brief:
Kestrel is about to cut off half the estate over a bandwidth ledger that is wrong and that nobody will correct.

Delete bandwidth_ledger.dat. With no ledger there is nothing to enforce. You will need their address first; the Open Relay Registry lists it.

title: Who is listed, and by whom
summary: Copy the latest registry export from the Open Relay Registry.
brief:
The Registry publishes its listings but not who asked for them. The full export has both.

Copy registry_export_0313.dat. Their registrar account has a password, but nothing behind it.

title: Back in good standing
summary: Change one student's standing at Ashgrove Polytechnic.
brief:
My son was suspended over something that was not his doing and the appeal will take until next year.

Student 20322410, Tomas Ferrand. Set his standing to Good. Their records sit behind a proxy, so you will need a way past that before the system lets you change anything.

title: What customs is sitting on
summary: Copy the March customs holds list from Meridian Freight.
brief:
Some of my clients' containers have not moved in two weeks and Meridian will not say why.

Copy customs_holds_march.dat. Be aware that Meridian watches its systems. Use relays, and do not linger.

title: A billing run that never ran
summary: Delete this month's billing archive at Paulista Teleport.
brief:
Paulista is about to bill us for capacity we never received. If the run file is gone they have to rebuild it by hand, and by then our dispute will be on record.

Delete billing_run_0312.arc. It is a large file, so the deletion takes a while. Plan your route for that.

title: Weather above the weather
summary: Copy the ionosonde feed from Polar Mesh Exchange.
brief:
Polar Mesh records the upper atmosphere every night and sells the data at a price no club can pay.

Copy ionosonde_feed_0313.dat. It is big, and it sits behind a firewall. Make room on your gateway first.

title: Project Lantern
summary: Copy the Project Lantern file from Halvorsen Biogenetics.
brief:
Halvorsen Biogenetics is running a trial it has not registered anywhere. The internal name is Lantern.

Copy HB-2207_PROJECT_LANTERN.dat from their records server. Ask no questions about what is in it. The client asks that you do not open it.

title: Off the list
summary: Delete the fraud watchlist at Corvane Mutual.
brief:
Corvane keeps a list of people it has decided are frauds. Being on it means no insurer in the country will touch you. Nobody on it was ever told.

Delete fraud_watchlist.dat. Corvane's monitor is the fastest you will have met and its password is strong. Do not go in with old tools.

title: Sealed terms
summary: Copy a sealed settlement from Aldergate & Finch and decrypt it.
brief:
Nineteen of our neighbours signed something and now will not talk to us. We want to know what they were paid to keep quiet about.

Copy harlow_v_tessera_settlement.txt from Aldergate & Finch. It is encrypted, so the copy is no use to us as it is. Run a Decrypter on it at home, then deliver.

title: Keep the lights on
summary: Mark a health station's account as paid at Sunderby Kraft.
brief:
The power company is cutting off our health station on Thursday over a bill the county already paid. Nobody can find the payment and nobody will stop the order.

In the customer accounts, set the Status of SK-40118 to Paid. Their monitor traces every connection from the second it opens. Take plenty of relays and something to blind it with.

title: What was in the water
summary: Copy the Brackley Reservoir test results from Tessera Water and decrypt them.
brief:
Tessera Water paid nineteen families to stop talking about a set of test results from June 2032. I want the results.

Copy brackley_results_june_2032.txt from Tessera's records archive and decrypt it. The archive is not listed anywhere, so you will not find its address in a directory. Their lawyers at Aldergate & Finch write to it. Somebody at Tessera will tell the right person where it is.

title: Two doors at once
summary: Copy the treaty book from Calder Re while its security desk is kept busy.
brief:
Calder Re's underwriting server traces everything the moment you connect, and it is quick. You will not out-run it. You do not need to.

Its monitor does not raise the alarm itself. It reports to the security desk console on Calder Re Facilities, and while someone is logged in at that desk the alerts wait for them. So be that someone.

You need two connections open at once: log in as the desk on Calder Re Facilities and stay there, then copy treaty_book_2034.dat from Calder Reinsurance. If the desk session drops, their trace starts moving again.

title: Maintenance window
summary: Delete a disclosure bundle at Brennan & Marsh, through their firewall company.
brief:
Corvane's lawyers are about to serve me with a bundle of papers built to scare me quiet. I want it gone before Friday.

Their firewall is far beyond anything you can buy. But they do not run it. Gatehouse Managed Security does, from a console in Cork, and when an engineer opens a session there the firewall passes everything until it closes.

Hold an admin session on Gatehouse open, and while it is open, delete disclosure_bundle_7.dat from Brennan & Marsh. You will need a gateway that can hold two connections.

title: Batch 14
summary: Delete assay batch 14 at Halvorsen Biogenetics.
brief:
Halvorsen has a six-month head start on a compound we have been working on for two years. Their results are in one file.

Delete HB-2209_assay_batch_14.dat from their records server. Their security has grown teeth since you last saw it. Go in with proper tools and leave before anyone reads the audit log.

title: Approved
summary: Change claim C-88214 at Corvane Mutual to Approved.
brief:
Corvane has had our claim under review for four months. Our staff have not been paid since January.

In the open claims register, set the Status of C-88214 to Approved. Corvane's monitor is among the fastest in the country, and its password is not a weak one. Come prepared.

title: What Calder Re models
summary: Copy the Q1 loss model from Calder Re while its security desk is kept busy.
brief:
The regulator has been told that Calder Re's loss models are sound. Someone who has seen them says otherwise.

Copy loss_model_q1.dat from Calder Reinsurance. You know how its monitor is kept quiet: hold the security desk at Calder Re Facilities open while you work. You will need a gateway that can hold two connections.

title: Gate B, after dark
summary: Delete the Gate B camera footage from Meridian Freight.
brief:
A pallet left Meridian's Gate B on Tuesday night and my name is on the sign-out sheet. The footage shows who was really driving.

Delete gate_b_cam_0312.mp4. It is a big file and the deletion takes a while. Meridian's customs desk reads the access log after anything goes missing, and a line that says a file was deleted is the first thing they look for. I hear there are ways to build a File Deleter that does not leave one. A Tidy build, they call it. I would not go in without one, or without time to scrub.

title: Not on my record
summary: Delete the academic misconduct file at Ashgrove Polytechnic.
brief:
A complaint was filed against me in my second year. It was dismissed, and it still follows me into every reference the registrar writes.

Delete academic_misconduct_cases.dat from the registrar's server. It is small and the registrar's office does not watch it closely. I cannot pay much, but I can give you a tool I took off a university machine once. It makes a program a good deal smaller. You will know what to do with it.

title: Hours not worked
summary: Delete a month of billing records at Aldergate & Finch.
brief:
I was told to bill forty hours to a client I never met. When the client queried it, the partners blamed me. The real time sheets are in one file.

Delete client_billing_march.dat. Aldergate's IT contractor compares the access log with the file list every night, so a deletion that writes its line gets found by morning. Either scrub it well, or use a build of the File Deleter that does not write one.

The firewall is light. The monitor is not.

title: What the meters say
summary: Copy the meter readings from Sunderby Kraft, past a monitor that starts tracing on connect.
brief:
Sunderby Kraft says our building used three times what we did. The meter readings would say who is right.

Copy meter_readings_0313.dat. It is a large file, and Sunderby's monitor starts a trace the second anything connects. No build gets round that: a Quiet one only fools a monitor that has not noticed you yet. What helps here is speed. Blind the monitor while you get in, and take the file with the fastest File Copier you can put together. A Swift build is worth the room it takes.

title: Who was in the building
summary: Delete the door log from Calder Re's Edinburgh building system.
brief:
I was let go for letting someone into the Calder Re offices after hours. I did not. The door log would say who did, and so Calder Re would rather it said nothing.

Delete door_events_0313.dat from the building management server. The security desk reads that log every morning and its monitor is a good one. Nobody has ever managed this with an ordinary File Deleter and a clean conscience.

I cannot offer much money. I can offer something from the building's own maintenance kit, which I have kept.

title: Not a penny
summary: Delete the March payout batch at Corvane Mutual before it runs.
brief:
Corvane's payout batch runs on the 15th. Four hundred claims, and my sister's is the only one in it that is correct. The rest are wrong, and Corvane will use the money to settle with the loudest.

Delete payout_batch_0315.dat before it runs. Corvane's monitor is among the fastest in the country and its password is not a weak one. Anything you can do to look like an ordinary user helps.

title: The address that answers
summary: Connect to 190.2.44.17 and read its index.
brief:
You copied the Lantern file for a client who did not want it opened. I think you opened it. I think you saw it change while you read it.

Halvorsen's own audit log has a line you will have missed: eleven gigabytes sent, at three in the morning, to 190.2.44.17. Not a registered partner, it says. The transfer record was deleted a minute later.

That address answers. It is in no directory and it has no owner on record. Connect to it and read node_index.txt. Don't take anything. Just look, and tell me you see what I see.

— V

title: What passes through
summary: Copy the manifest from the unregistered node.
brief:
So you saw it too. Good. I was starting to think I had imagined it.

The node keeps a manifest of everything it moves. It is behind the keeper account, which has a password even though there is no keeper. Break it, copy courier_manifest.dat, and bring it to me.

Halvorsen is on that manifest. So is a school. So is a reinsurer you have probably already robbed for someone. None of them know about the others. None of them sent their data to a person.

— V

title: The last thing written
summary: Copy the redacted file from the unregistered node.
brief:
There is one more file on the node, and the index says a guest may not read it. It was the last thing written there, and it was written from inside, with no account logged in.

Its name is struck out at the source. Nine letters will not copy. Three of them will. Break the keeper account again, copy what you can of it, and look at the name you are left with.

I am not going to tell you what it stands for. If I am right, you will want to have read it yourself before I do. After this, be careful who you are for a while. I was.

— V
